La4Ni3O10 single crystals were successfully grown using the high-pressure optical floating-zone technique under 20 bar oxygen pressure.
Two distinct phases, P21/a and Bmab, were obtained through different growth and post-annealing processes.
The metal-to-metal transition occurred at 152 K for the Bmab structure and 136 K for the P21/a structure.
The magnetic susceptibility data showed sharp anomalies at the metal-to-metal transition temperatures, indicating excellent crystallinity and phase purity.
The analysis of the magnetization data suggested the presence of quasi-free spins in the ≲ 1 ‰-regime, assuming localized moments with S = 1.
The specific heat capacity measurements showed sharp anomalies at the metal-to-metal transition temperatures, allowing the quantification of the associated entropy changes.
The data implied insignificant effects of magnetic field on the metal-to-metal transition temperature, which was experimentally confirmed.
The authors' crystals showed slightly different ordering temperatures compared to previously reported single crystals and polycrystals, which was attributed to differences in oxygen stoichiometry.
The absence of the previously reported ferromagnetic impurity phase in the authors' crystals confirmed its extrinsic nature.
The key parameters for successful crystal growth were the use of 20 bar oxygen pressure, the optimization of the feed and seed rod velocities, and the rapid cooling of the as-grown boule.
The post-annealing process under oxygen pressure led to a notable reduction of the impurity phase in the crystals.
The Bmab structure was found to be the as-grown phase, while the P21/a structure was obtained after the high-pressure annealing process.
The specific heat and magnetic susceptibility anomalies were much sharper in the authors' crystals compared to previously reported data, indicating excellent crystallinity.

The entropy changes associated with the metal-to-metal transition were by ca. 20% smaller than found for single crystals reported in the literature and ca. 40% larger than for a P21/a-structured polycrystal.
The authors' results confirm the thermodynamic stability of the P21/a structure and the transformation of the Bmab structure to P21/a upon heat treatment.
